subject: Dedicated capacity decision: GPU selector & concurrency next steps
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@novaretail.com>, DevOps Team <devops@novaretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity decision: GPU selector & concurrency next steps

Hi Sara / DevOps,

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and the follow-ups we promised:

- Deployment preference: you mentioned wanting customer isolation and predictable latency for checkout fraud prevention, so Dedicated capacity looks like the right first step (we also noted Private/VPC later for compliance gating).
- Key unknowns for us to size correctly: expected peak TPS, steady-state TPS, average/peak prompt lengths (tokens in / tokens out), desired concurrency window (how many simultaneous requests must be <250ms), and whether you need HSM/KMS integrations for keys.

Action items (proposed):
1) You: share a short token-profile (sample prompt lengths + % distribution) and any SLOs (p95/p99 latency targets).
2) Us: propose a 2-option GPU recommendation (cost-optimized vs latency-optimized) and a short benchmark plan we can run on a sanitized sample.
3) Joint: schedule a 30-min bench kickoff next week and agree test dataset & success criteria.

I attached a quick capacity worksheet (capacity-worksheet-v1.xlsx) with the fields we usually need — filling the highlighted rows will let us produce an accurate TPS->GPU mapping.

If Dedicated makes sense you can expect two realistic GPU choices for a production pool: A100-style (cost-efficient for high multiplexing) or H100-style (better single-request latency / larger KV cache). I’ll loop Ben for the kernel/runtime tradeoffs.

Thanks — available tomorrow 10:30–12:00 PT if that works for a short sync.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks Mateo — great summary.

Quick answers:
- Peak TPS (checkout enrichment): ~120 TPS sustained short bursts (5–10 min), baseline steady ~15 TPS.
- Concurrency target: support 3–5 concurrent sessions at sub-250ms p95.
- Token mix: median prompt ~120 tokens, median completion ~60 tokens. Distribution: 60% short (<=80 tokens), 30% medium (81–250), 10% long (>250).
- Data sensitivity: payloads include PII fields (hashed customer IDs). For now we prefer Dedicated with private network peering; long-term goal is Private/VPC for full isolation.

Attached: our token-profile export (sara_novaretail_token_profile.json) — sanitized sample and a short histogram.

We’re happy to run your benchmark on sanitized traffic. Tuesday (Apr 13) afternoon PT works for our DevOps.

—Sara
Sara Chen
Head of AI Platform, NovaRetail
sara.chen@novaretail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Sara Chen <sara.chen@novaretail.com>, DevOps Team <devops@novaretail.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity decision: GPU selector & concurrency next steps

Putting some engineering context on Mateo’s recap so we can converge on options:

1) GPU candidates
   - A100-80GB pool (many-model multiplex): better utilization if you have many concurrent small requests; lower per-token cost when we can multiplex and use quantization. Good if 60% of requests are short.
   - H100-80GB pool (latency-first): better for p95 sub-250ms for medium/long completions, larger KV cache for long-context use cases. Higher hourly cost but fewer nodes for the same latency SLO.

2) Concurrency / batching knobs
   - With 3–5 concurrency and median length ~120 tokens, smart continuous batching should get you good token economics on A100. For H100, we can prioritize single-request latency and smaller batch windows.

3) Benchmark ask (what we need from NovaRetail)
   - 300–500 sanitized requests representative of short/medium/long buckets (your token_profile covers this)
   - A sample of the heaviest request pattern (peak) to validate burst behavior
   - Prefer a flagged sandbox key or short-lived tokens — we will not store payloads.

4) Metrics we’ll report back
   - p50/p95/p99 latency breakouts, tokens/s, effective throughput, cost per 1M tokens for each GPU pool, and a suggested ops plan (pool size + autoscale bands).

If you confirm the sample dataset and Tuesday afternoon bench slot, I’ll prepare two bench configs (A100-optimized, H100-optimized) and an ops runbook that shows scaling behavior.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
